definition.OPT_i: the value of R_i if and only if an upper bound closes the gap (U_i == R_i); otherwise null
definition.R_i: best feasible cut found by the diverse heuristic ensemble; the authoritative value is the integer recomputed from graph.json + partition.json by tools/verify_partition.py, never MQLib's own reported objective
definition.U_i: minimum of the rigorous upper bounds actually computed (spectral eigenvalue bound, SDP/Delorme-Poljak dual bound)
definition.lower_bound_warning: a feasible cut is a LOWER bound on the optimum; it is never an upper bound

provenance.artifacts_note: Binaries are NOT vendored into this repository (575 KB). The sha256 above identifies the exact executable that produced targets.json; rebuild with build/build_mqlib.sh. A different compiler may produce a different binary and, in principle, a different R_i; the source pin plus flags are the reproducible identity.
provenance.patches_note: none: the working tree was clean at build time (git status --porcelain empty) and no source file was edited. The graph.json -> MQLib conversion lives in our own tools/to_mqlib.py, not in a patch to upstream.
provenance.reported_vs_recomputed: MQLib's own objective line is recorded per run in logs/runs/*.json as mqlib_reported_objective, purely as a cross-check. The authoritative value is the integer recomputed from graph.json + partition.json by tools/verify_partition.py.

source_digest.method: sha256 over the sorted `sha256sum` output of every src/**/*.cpp and include/**/*.h

ensemble.seeds_note: five fixed seeds spread over MQLib's 0..65535 seed range; MQLib's time-based termination makes an individual run non-reproducible in principle, but R_i is a maximum over runs and is reported together with the partitions that witness it
